changelog.change: Added the mediawiki-xml reader kind and its pageNamespace knob, required on that kind and forbidden on every other.
changelog.why: Row 4b - the Tamil Wiktionary CONTENT dump is a MediaWiki export, a format none of the three existing readers can stream. Which namespace holds the records is a property of the export rather than of the format (a dump interleaves articles with talk, template and project pages), so it is declared per source like hasHeader rather than assumed in the reader.

changelog.change: Added attestationTier, required on every source whose role may assert word-hood and forbidden on every other.
changelog.why: Row 9a - whether a source's UNIT is a lexicographic ENTRY or a bare listing is a property of the SOURCE, and the classifier's headword gate needs it per source rather than re-derived per row. It is a declared field rather than a Python literal or a hardcoded id list (Holy Law #6) so registering the next authority forces the ruling instead of silently inheriting one.

changelog.change: Initial lexicon source registry: per-source role, precedence, sha256 and reader mapping across the delimited / json-array / jsonl kinds, plus the POS and category alias maps.
changelog.why: Row 3 - contracts before logic (Holy Law #3). elementKind lands in the initial mint rather than with the readers: two acquired sources hold bare string array elements, and reopening a contract three rows after it shipped is a Holy Law #3 inversion.

Nouns.note: The curated themed source files parts of speech as categories on 827 of its 1,290 rows. It is a real classification over a hand-checked set, unlike the blanket 'nouns' stamp below.

art.note: Describes the English headword. Tamil has no article in any form, so the Tamil side's part of speech is simply unknown.

n.pl.note: Two facts in one tag: it is a noun, and the form carried is a plural rather than the lemma. Each goes to its own home.

nouns.note: The curated master dictionary stamps this on 104,221 of its 104,421 rows (99.8 percent), verbs included, so as the source uses it the value classifies nothing. Counted over the whole file on 2026-08-15; its four real tags - trees, flowers, birds, animals - route to categoryAliases.

prep.note: The label describes the ENGLISH headword; the Tamil side of all 34 rows is Tamil's own adposition, which is postpositional.

rel.note: One row, the relative sense of English 'but'. Tamil expresses it with a verbal form rather than a word class.

\u0b87\u0b9f\u0bc8\u0b9a\u0bcd\u0b9a\u0b.note: idaicchol. The six Tamil-script tags below are the Tamil Wiktionary's own grammatical vocabulary, written as escapes so a decomposed literal cannot silently match nothing. Its abbreviations and plurals are folded onto these six by the reader that knows that source, exactly as the English-Tamil dictionary's fourteen prefix spellings fold onto twelve tags.

sources.name: Curated themed Tamil vocabulary with English pairings
sources.note: The cleanest theme plus one-word-English pairing on disk, hand-checked across 1,290 rows, so it takes the highest precedence for a single-slot English translation. role=category, so it never asserts word-hood.

sources.name: Tamil Wiktionary via Wiktextract (kaikki.org)
sources.note: Modern coverage the 1930s lexicons lack, with senses and synonyms. Its 'categories' are Wiktionary maintenance buckets rather than themes, so no categoryField is mapped.

sources.name: English-Tamil dictionary with part-of-speech prefixes (t1)
sources.note: No rootKey: the document ROOT is the array. Read forward each Tamil term translates to the row's English headword; read sideways the terms filed under one (English headword, part of speech) are a synonym set.

sources.name: yen-tamizh_OLD curated Tamil master dictionary
sources.note: Its English field is measured unreliable (edu -> 'almagest', kayal -> 'dare'), so it sits below every other translation producer. Kept because it is the only source carrying both counts and themed tags.

sources.name: Tamil word list validated by a Nannul-rules spellchecker
sources.note: 355,275 bare strings - a ready-made orthotactic signal, and the reason elementKind admits 'string' at all.

sources.name: Clean Tamil word list (HuggingFace derived)
sources.note: Independent attestation of modern vocabulary, also bare strings.

sources.name: yen-tamizh_OLD raw Tamil word list (t2)
sources.note: Attestation only, no counts. Its 8,686 underscore-joined phrases are kept like every other surface; the classifier decides what they are, not the reader.

sources.name: Cleaned Tamil inflected verb forms
sources.note: One form per line. The delimiter is nominal - a tab never occurs, so the whole line is column 0 and the surface reaches the store verbatim.

sources.name: Bulk Tamil inflected verb forms
sources.note: 1,461,494 forms, one per line. role=formEvidence, so it can only ever assert that a surface is NOT a headword.

sources.name: OpenSubtitles 2018 Tamil frequency list (hermitdave/FrequencyWords)
sources.note: Subtitle Tamil is spoken Tamil. It is the numerator of spokenRatio, which is why it leads the frequency block.

sources.name: Aggregated Tamil web and news word frequency
sources.note: 188 MB and the richest single frequency signal. It is the source the streaming rule exists for.

sources.name: Deduplicated Tamil web corpus word frequency
Tamil Murasu news archive 2011-2020 word frequency
sirukathaigal.com short-story archive word frequency
sources.note: Named .html upstream but the bytes are word,count lines - a path-and-mapping decision, not a code one.

sources.name: azhiyasudargal.com word frequency
sources.note: DISABLED: the extraction that produced it stripped vowel signs and pulli, so its tokens are bare consonant skeletons - valid Tamil letters that are not Tamil words, and some of which cannot begin a Tamil word at all. Registered and explained rather than deleted, so nobody re-adds it in a year having forgotten why it went. Flip it on only if a corrected extraction replaces the bytes, which would change its sha256.

sources.name: Agent-authored Tamil meanings, synonyms, translations, POS and themes
sources.origin: authored in-session by the agent executing the pipeline; see docs/how-to/enrich-the-lexicon.md
sources.note: The only source whose bytes are COMMITTED rather than acquired, and the only one whose reader validates a shape: see wordsmith/llm_enrich.py. Last precedence on purpose - an authored English translation must lose the single display slot to every attested one. No posField or categoryField is mapped: an authored row writes the closed pos and category vocabularies natively, so it has no raw orthography for posAliases or categoryAliases to translate.

sources.name: Tamil Wiktionary page titles, main namespace
sources.note: A TIER-2, enumerative authority: every row is a bare page title, with no gloss, definition, part of speech, synonym or category anywhere in the dump, so it can never satisfy the entry test and cannot make a surface a headword on its own. The delimiter is a tab, which the file never contains, so each line yields the whole title as one column. It is deliberately NOT the underscore the dump uses for a space: splitting there would attest the first word of a multi-word page, and a multi-word entry attests the phrase, not the words inside it. Precedence last because a title list has no English gloss to win the single display slot with, and renumbering thirteen sources for a value that never competes would be churn.

sources.name: Tamil Wiktionary articles, main namespace
sources.note: The same wiki as ta-wiktionary-titles, and the opposite tier, because the CONTENT is what the title list does not carry: a Tamil sense, a synonym set, a part of speech, an English gloss. That description IS the editorial act attestationTier names, so this source is lexicographic where the bare title list is enumerative. Its headword fact is emitted only for a page that carries at least one of those facts - a stub with nothing said about it is observed, never attested, so the tier-1 claim is true row by row and not merely on average. Precedence last: the wiki's translation column is a free-text list one editor at a time, and it must lose the single English display slot to every curated dictionary.
